title: UEFI PE32+ Image Loading
description: Loads bootloaders as PE32+ executables through the firmware's LoadImage service. The image carries relocations and a proper subsystem type so the firmware can place it anywhere in memory. It is the fundamental unit of UEFI boot.
key_mechanisms: Build the loader as a PE32+ image

demo.title: Demo — UEFI PE32+ Image Loading

title: Graphics Output Protocol Setup
description: Uses the Graphics Output Protocol for framebuffer access before any OS driver loads. The bootloader queries available modes, picks the native resolution, and draws progress UI directly. It replaces legacy VGA text mode entirely.
key_mechanisms: Query modes and pick native resolution

demo.title: Demo — Graphics Output Protocol Setup

title: Boot Services Memory Management
description: Manages the transition from firmware boot services to OS runtime by exiting boot services cleanly. The loader collects the memory map, calls ExitBootServices, and never touches firmware services again. Getting the map key right is the classic pitfall.
key_mechanisms: Collect the memory map with the map key
Never call boot services after exit

demo.title: Demo — Boot Services Memory Management

title: Secure Boot Chain
description: Verifies each boot stage's signature against keys in the firmware database before executing it. Platform Key to Key Exchange Key to signature database forms the chain of trust. Only signed loaders run when Secure Boot is on.

demo.title: Demo — Secure Boot Chain

title: ESP Partition Layout
description: Lays out the EFI System Partition with the standard directory structure firmware expects. The FAT32 partition holds loaders under EFI/BOOT and EFI/<vendor>, plus fallback binaries. Correct layout is what makes removable media boot anywhere.

demo.title: Demo — ESP Partition Layout

title: ACPI Table Handoff
description: Passes ACPI tables from firmware to the OS for power management and device discovery. The loader locates the RSDP via the configuration table and hands the pointer to the kernel. Broken ACPI is the classic cause of boot hangs.
key_mechanisms: Find RSDP in the config table
Pass the pointer to the kernel

demo.title: Demo — ACPI Table Handoff

title: UEFI Memory Map Parsing
description: Parses the firmware memory map to learn which regions are usable RAM. The loader walks descriptors, merges adjacent conventional memory, and reserves firmware-reserved ranges. The OS memory manager is seeded from this map.

demo.title: Demo — UEFI Memory Map Parsing

title: Boot Manager Variables
description: Manages BootOrder and Boot#### NVRAM variables that define the boot menu. Each entry points to a loader path on the ESP with optional parameters. Tools like efibootmgr edit them from the OS.

demo.title: Demo — Boot Manager Variables

title: PXE Network Boot
description: Boots over the network using the firmware's PXE stack: DHCP for the address, TFTP for the loader. Diskless machines boot a full OS image fetched at power-on. It is how datacenters provision thousands of bare-metal nodes.
key_mechanisms: DHCP to discover the boot server

demo.title: Demo — PXE Network Boot

title: Shim First-Stage Loading
description: Uses the shim first-stage loader, signed by Microsoft's CA, to bridge Secure Boot to distro-signed kernels. Shim verifies the second stage against the distro key (MOK) the user enrolled. It is how Linux boots on Secure Boot PCs.

demo.title: Demo — Shim First-Stage Loading

title: Measured Boot with TPM
description: Extends TPM platform configuration registers with each boot component's hash, creating a tamper-evident boot log. Remote attestation can then verify exactly what booted. Unlike Secure Boot it does not block — it records.

demo.title: Demo — Measured Boot with TPM

title: Capsule Update Delivery
description: Delivers firmware updates as UEFI capsules processed on the next reboot. The OS stages the capsule; firmware applies it before boot services start. It standardizes firmware updates across vendors.
key_mechanisms: Stage the capsule from the OS

demo.title: Demo — Capsule Update Delivery

title: Boot Variable Redundancy
description: Keeps redundant copies of critical boot variables so a failed update cannot brick the boot path. Firmware writes variables atomically with a journal; on corruption it falls back to the last good set. It is the safety net under firmware updates.

demo.title: Demo — Boot Variable Redundancy

title: DXE Driver Binding
description: Binds Driver Execution Environment drivers to controllers during the DXE phase. The dispatcher topologically sorts drivers by dependency and binds them to PCI, USB, and storage controllers. It is where hardware becomes usable to the firmware.
key_mechanisms: Dispatch DXE drivers in dependency order

demo.title: Demo — DXE Driver Binding

title: Fallback Boot Paths
description: Falls back through removable-media paths and BootOrder entries when the primary loader fails. The firmware tries each entry in order, ending at the default removable path. It is why a USB stick boots even with a broken internal install.
key_mechanisms: Fall back to removable media paths

demo.title: Demo — Fallback Boot Paths
